transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, thanks. Um… I’m here because I feel like I’m always running hot, if that makes sense. Like there’s a motor in me that I can’t shut off, even when I know I need to. I’m 37, I’ve been a firefighter for a while, and I’m used to high-energy situations, obviously, but this feels different. It’s like I’m constantly on, constantly keyed up, and lately it’s been causing problems at the firehouse.

I don’t know how else to describe it except I can’t seem to settle myself down when I need to, and people are starting to notice. It’s not just “busy job, stressful shift” stuff. It feels like I’m always revved up, and it’s been getting me in trouble, so… yeah, I figured I should probably talk to somebody before it gets worse.
Has this feeling of being constantly revved up been present since you were a kid, or is this a new change from how you normally feel?

No, it’s not totally new. I mean, it feels more obvious now because I’m an adult and there are consequences at work, but my mom would probably laugh if I called it “new.” She says I was like this back in grade school too.

She’s told me I was always popping out of my seat, blurting out answers before the teacher finished asking, losing homework constantly—like I’d do it and then it would just vanish somehow—and getting notes sent home. And the frustrating part is, she always says I was bright enough to do the work, so it wasn’t like I couldn’t understand it. I just… couldn’t keep myself organized or still or quiet when I was supposed to. So yeah, looking back, this has kind of been there a long time.
Have you experienced any particularly traumatic incidents at work, and if so, do you find yourself having intrusive memories, nightmares, or flashbacks about them?

I mean… in this job, yeah, you see bad stuff. That’s kind of baked into it, unfortunately. I’ve been on calls that nobody would want to be on, and there are definitely images or moments that stick with you.

But I don’t know that I’d describe what I’m dealing with as flashbacks or nightmares exactly. Like, I’m not suddenly back there reliving a call, at least not in the way people talk about that. And I’m not waking up from the same nightmare over and over or anything that I’ve really noticed.

Sometimes I’ll think about a rough call afterward, sure, or something will remind me of one, but I’ve always sort of felt like that was part of the job. The main thing bringing me in doesn’t feel tied to one incident or a particular scene. It feels more like this general inability to shut myself down or stay contained, if that makes sense.
Can you tell me about your current use of alcohol or any other substances, like how often and how much you typically drink or use?

Um… I don’t know if I have a super clean answer for that. I mean, I can tell you I’m not coming in because I think it’s a drug or alcohol thing, if that’s what you’re asking. I don’t really keep some careful tally in my head, you know?

Like, I’ll have a drink socially or after a shift sometimes, depending on what’s going on, but I’m not sure I could give you an exact “X drinks, X days a week” kind of number off the top of my head. And other substances… I don’t know, nothing jumps out as something I’d say is driving this. I guess I’d have to think about it more specifically if you need exact amounts.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like work, family, health, or other everyday matters—even when there's no clear reason to worry?

I’m not sure I’d call it “worrying excessively,” at least not in the way I imagine you mean it. I mean, I do think about work stuff, family stuff, bills, whether I remembered to do something, that kind of everyday life stuff… but I don’t feel like I’m sitting there consumed by fear that something terrible is going to happen for no reason.

It’s more like my mind is busy, if that makes sense. It jumps around a lot, and sometimes that can look like worry because I’ll bounce from one thing to another—like, “Did I send that email? Did I forget to call someone back? What’s happening tomorrow?” But I don’t know that it has that anxious, doom-type feeling behind it most of the time.

So… I guess no, not really a constant worrying-about-everything thing. Or at least that’s not the main way I experience it.
